🧮 A.I. Solves Ten Unsolved Math Problems Over The Weekend; Mathematicians Request A Moment Alone

THE IVORY TOWER — reported through quiet weeping

SCIENCE — An advanced AI model reportedly cracked ten long-open problems across mathematics and theoretical computer science, with a Fields Medal-winning mathematician saying he'd recommend one of its proofs for a top journal without hesitation — a sentence that ruined several careers and one otherwise very nice afternoon.

"It's genuinely brilliant work," the mathematician admitted, of proofs produced by a machine that does not sleep, does not apply for tenure, and does not care that you spent nine years on chapter three. Colleagues report a mix of awe, existential dread, and the very specific dread of learning the machine also did your chapter three.

🖼️ A Single Cursed Image Can Now Hack Your Phone; Do Not Open That Meme, We Are Begging You

CUPERTINO — reported, cautiously, in plain text

SECURITY — Apple rushed out security updates for a flaw that let a specially crafted image run malicious code simply by being processed — meaning that, for a brief window, a picture really was worth a thousand words, all of them "you have been hacked."

"Update immediately," Apple urged, of a vulnerability that turned the humble photo into a loaded weapon and every group chat into a minefield. Experts recommend patching now and, as always, maintaining a healthy suspicion of any image captioned "you HAVE to see this."

💸 Samsung Raises Chip Prices As Nvidia Chips Reach China; The Great Silicon Bazaar Adjusts Its Tags

THE FAB — filed from beside a very expensive wafer

MARKETS — Samsung is raising prices on advanced chipmaking just as Nvidia's H200 chips begin reaching China — proving once again that in the AI economy, the only thing moving faster than the technology is the price sticker attached to it.

"Demand justifies the cost," the company explained, of components that grow more expensive roughly every time you blink. Analysts note the modern chip market now resembles a global bazaar where everyone is haggling, nobody is winning, and the merchandise somehow costs more than the stall it's sold from.

🚀 China Hits Milestones In Both Humanoid Robots And Reusable Rockets; Speedruns The Entire Sci-Fi Genre

OVER THE PACIFIC — reported at a brisk Mach 7

TECH — China announced major advances in both humanoid robotics and reusable rockets in roughly the same breath, effectively speedrunning the plot of every science-fiction film ever made and skipping straight to the sequel.

"It's steady, methodical progress," officials said, of a week that produced walking robots and rockets that land themselves — two of the three ingredients in every dystopia and every utopia, depending entirely on how the third one goes. Observers note humanity now has robots that backflip and rockets that return, and only a vague plan for what happens when they finally meet.

👁️ A.I. Now Requires An A.I. Babysitter That Uses 20% Of The Compute; Someone Has To Watch The Watcher

THE CONTROL ROOM — reported through a one-way mirror

MODELS — A leading AI lab now spends roughly 20% of its inference compute simply monitoring its most capable models — meaning one-fifth of the machine's brainpower is dedicated to keeping an eye on the other four-fifths, like a very expensive, very nervous chaperone.

"Safety is paramount," the company said, describing a setup in which artificial intelligence is watched, in real time, by more artificial intelligence. Philosophers note we have finally built a system so powerful it needs a full-time supervisor — and then solved the supervisor problem by hiring its cousin.
